To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimal dietary supply amino acids for maintenance, growth and carcass accretion in broilers can be determined by measuring the amino acid intake and accretion at different growth rates and body weights and using the slope of the regression of amino acid intake on amino acid accretions to calculate the optimal amino acid supply for any growth rate and body weight.
the amino acid intake required to maximize the efficiency of utilization for growth is linearly related to the growth rate of the bird.
amino acid requirements for maintenance and growth were measured in a broiler strain and that these requirements can be used to calculate optimal amino acid supply to maximize growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the optimal amino acid supply to broilers.
the determination of optimal amino acids intake for maintenance and gain in the Ross 308 chicks.
the direct determination of amino acid requirement for growth and maintenance in broilers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amino acid requirements of the Ross 308 broiler chick are higher than previously reported, and the requirements are higher for maintenance than for growth.
amino acid intake for growth is not a function of protein intake.
the results of this study have shown that the NRC (2005) recommendations for amino acid supply are generally too low, but the recommendations for threonine are adequate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
amino acid requirements for growth are higher then those recommended in the Ross 308 manual, but are lower then those recommended in NRC (1991).
the optimal supply of amino acids is greater then the NRC recommendations and that the amino acid requirements of broiler chicks are similar to those of other poultry species.
the optimal dietary supply for maintenance and growth was higher then the current NRC (1993) and Ross recommendations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal dietary amino acid requirements for growth are higher than the current empirical recommendations.
amino acids are not interchangeable and that amino acids are required in specific amounts.
the amino acid requirements for broiler chickens should be calculated as a function of body weight.
